title: State projection belongs in DontPanic core; sync layers are adapters
body: Architectural critique on 2026-05-09 sharpened the boundary between DontPanic platform and adapter ecosystem. DontPanic was about to grow Firestore-specific sync code as part of plan 2026-05-03-002 F004. The cleaner shape: DontPanic emits a single normalized state contract (this plan); adapters consume it (sibling plan feat-team-dashboard-sync). This keeps DontPanic neutral across deployment shapes — Firestore today, SQL or Postgres or KV tomorrow, none privileged. It also gives U8 (external orchestrator) and U9 (CI reviewer) a stable subscription point without each adapter learning the filesystem layout.

title: Read-only by default; mutations stay on existing MCP approval semantics
body: The projection is strictly read. Adapters that need to fire approvals or dispatch volleys call the existing mutation tools (`approve_gate`, `dispatch`, `resume`, `read_evidence`) which already require `confirm: true` and surface to the user before executing. We do NOT add new mutation paths in this plan — that would let adapters drift toward bypassing operator approval. Mutation goes through MCP; projection is for state visibility.

title: Three redaction levels: public / operator / full
body: Per the role/action matrix in USE_CASES.md, dashboards serving Observer roles (CI status checks, public-channel posts, unauth viewers) need a strict redaction level. Operators using the local CLI need full state for debugging. Adapters serving authenticated operators need a middle level. Three discrete levels: `public` (Observer — no quota detail, no operator email, no supervisor PIDs, no file paths beyond plan_id), `operator` (default — full state minus secrets), `full` (CLI-only, never via MCP). MCP `state_snapshot` caps redaction at `operator` regardless of caller request — the `full` escape hatch is for direct local CLI invocations only.

title: Stable IDs over internal SHAs in projection
body: Plan IDs (`2026-05-09-003-feat-state-projection-v0`), feature IDs (`F001`–`F006`), gate names (`pre_impl`, `pre_merge`, `breaker:budget_ceiling`), and supervisor entries (PID + start time) are stable across DontPanic refactors and across schema bumps. Audit envelope SHAs and other internal-detail identifiers are NOT part of the projection — those stay in audit envelopes for in-DontPanic provenance and are not adapter-stable. This protects adapters from breaking when DontPanic refactors internals.

title: Schema versioning lives in agent-conventions, NOT in DontPanic repo
body: The `state-snapshot.schema.json` is a contract between DontPanic and any adapter ecosystem. Putting it in agent-conventions (already the home of plan/features/audit/signoff schemas) means: (a) one schema home for all DontPanic contracts, (b) version bumps follow agent-conventions discipline (semver, D-entries, deprecation periods), (c) adapters in different repos pin against the same canonical version, (d) DontPanic doesn't fork the schema for its own purposes. agent-conventions is currently v1.x; this adds the new schema at the next minor bump.

title: Stream selection happens at gather time, not just CLI flag
body: `state_projection.gather()` accepts `--include` so callers requesting just `plans, gates` skip the heavier `inbox` and `decisions` walks. This matters for adapters polling at high frequency (a dashboard refreshing every 5s shouldn't reread every plan's INBOX.md). The CLI flag is a thin pass-through to the function-level filter; both are equivalent in observable behavior.

title: Static projection-backed dashboard belongs in DontPanic core; only Firebase realtime is an adapter
body: Verification on 2026-05-10 found that DontPanic already ships a local-first static dashboard at DontPanic/dashboard/ — core.js:1 documents "Local-first: reads state from JSON files, no Firebase dependency." Five page modules (mission-control-logic, command-center-logic, security-logic, financial-logic, cloud-costs-logic, settings-logic) consume dashboard/state/*.json. firebase.json hosts the dashboard via Firebase Hosting but Hosting is just a static-file CDN — runtime has no Firebase dependency. Updated boundary: static, projection-backed dashboard belongs in DontPanic (OSS-friendly, works on any static host, every operator gets a dashboard immediately). The Firebase realtime team dashboard remains an adapter (sibling plan 2026-05-09-004, renamed to feat-firebase-dashboard-adapter-v0). Net F007 added here for the static consumer + export-dashboard CLI; the adapter plan reframes as the OPTIONAL realtime upgrade.

title: Plan locked: status:draft → active; goal_type=infra (not new_feature)
body: Pre-lock validation flagged that goal_type=new_feature would require an objective_contract document (Goal Governance V1 invariant). State projection is more accurately infrastructure: a substrate contract for adapters (dashboards, brokers, CI runners, hosted agents), not a user-facing feature. Changed goal_type from new_feature → infra. Same pattern as plans 2026-05-08-003 (harness frictions v1) and 2026-05-09-002 (verdict/status/env-blocker). Plan validates green against agent-conventions v1.0 schemas. Locked at 2026-05-10. Pre-lock ROADMAP.md updated to reference plans 003 + 004 as the next-up substrate work. Per-feature documentation updates (CONFIGURATION.md state commands, AGENT_QUICKSTART.md state_snapshot tool, dashboard/README.md, STATE_PROJECTION.md adapter governance) are inside features F004/F005/F006/F007 — they ship as part of the implementation, not pre-lock.

title: F001 closed: state-snapshot schema + Pydantic model land in agent-conventions v1.6.0
body: F001 schema lives at agent-conventions/schemas/v1.0/state-snapshot.schema.json (committed 4cd47e0, tagged v1.6.0). Auto-generated Pydantic model at claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/models/state_snapshot_model.py (StateSnapshot root + 7 sub-classes per stream). 21 new tests in scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_state_snapshot_schema_f001.py cover schema shape pins (8), Pydantic round-trip (5), schema rejection on malformed input (6), and agent-conventions VERSION pin (1) — all green. Full orchestrate sweep: 1699 passed, 7 skipped (no regressions). Two pre-existing tests updated to match v1.6.0 reality: VERSION pin in test_plan_surfaces_field.py bumped to 1.6.0; campaign-id references in docs/USE_CASES.md + docs/ROADMAP.md replaced with <your-firebase-project> placeholder per sanitization_check.py policy (operator-specific project IDs belong in ~/.dontpanic/projects.json, not OSS-facing marketing docs). Stable-ID discipline pinned in schema $description: plan_id format YYYY-MM-DD-NNN-type-slug, feature_id ^F\d{3}$, decision_id ^D\d{3}$, supervisor_id composite <pid>:<started_at>. Three redact_level values (public/operator/full) enum-pinned. Seven streams required: plans/gates/inbox/supervisors/quota/decisions/evidence_refs. Schema rejects extra top-level properties (additionalProperties:false at both top + streams).

title: Adopt Printing Press flag vocabulary in F004/F005 without adopting the generator
body: Researched mvanhorn/cli-printing-press (1410★, MIT, very active) and mvanhorn/printing-press-library. PP generates Go CLI + MCP binary pairs from OpenAPI / HAR / sniffed traffic. Concluded it does NOT fit the F004/F005 use case: (a) input is OpenAPI not JSON Schema — we have a JSON Schema for the state envelope, not an HTTP API; (b) output is Go — forks our Python runtime in scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/; (c) no built-in primitives for our policy-bearing surface (redact tiers, approve_gate semantics, project-registry safe paths, INBOX-first mutations); (d) defaults to HTTP transport which violates D003 local-only invariant of mcp_server.py. However the agent-flag vocabulary PP normalizes (--json/--compact/--select/--dry-run, typed exit codes) is becoming the de facto standard for agent-driven CLIs. F004 + F005 amended to add --compact and --select (jsonpath, read-only) so PP-trained agents drive `dontpanic state` without per-command relearning. Transport stays stdio-only. Tool naming stays domain-specific (state_snapshot, approve_gate, dispatch). MCP server stays Python in-process so policy stays at the tool boundary. ROADMAP Phase C entry sharpened: PP becomes the prescribed pattern for wrapping external SaaS (Linear/Sentry/Slack/Notion) — not a substitute for DontPanic's own CLI/MCP. Note: Printing-press-as-a-platform-skill is the bigger insight (raised post-amend); deferred to a separate plan (see D011 candidate) per scope-change protocol.

title: F002 closed: state_projection.gather() module + 23 fixture tests
body: state_projection.gather(plans_root, *, redact_level='operator', include=ALL_STREAMS, plan_id=None, ...) -> StateSnapshot at scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/state_projection.py. Seven per-stream gatherers (_gather_plans / _gather_gates / _gather_inbox / _gather_supervisors / _gather_quota / _gather_decisions / _gather_evidence_refs). Pure-read invariant enforced: tests fingerprint plans-tree mtime+size hash pre/post call, must match. Three design choices to note: (1) Active supervisors call list_active(prune=False) — list_active default prune=True rewrites the registry to remove dead-pid entries, which violates pure-read; tests use os.getpid() to ensure live entries. (2) Window mapping for quota: rolling_5h → daily, rolling_7d → weekly, rolling_30d → monthly; documented in _WINDOW_MAPPING constant. (3) redact_level is accepted and threaded into the returned snapshot but otherwise no-op in F002 — F003 owns the actual filtering policy. Test fixtures: 23 cases covering envelope shape (3), plans stream (3), gates stream (2), inbox stream (2), supervisors stream (2), quota stream (2), decisions stream (1), evidence_refs stream (1), include filter (2), plan_id filter (1), pure-read invariant (1), redact_level threading (2), graceful missing artifacts (1). Inbox fixture uses inbox.append_event() to match canonical INBOX.md format rather than hand-rolling. Evidence_refs gather uses model_dump(mode='json') to convert plan_model.Type enum → str for cross-model re-validation against state_snapshot_model.Type. Full sweep: 1722 passed, 7 skipped, zero regressions.
